building_blocks.name: Workflow Maps
building_blocks.what: See the shape of the work: each main process left to right, with its sub-processes branching off. Click any box for details.
building_blocks.source: playbook/, product-framework.md, RM memo Appendix B

building_blocks.name: Agent Library
building_blocks.what: Every agent in one place: what it does, what it may and may not do, and who's in charge. Filter by step or by who it serves.

building_blocks.name: Steps Catalog
building_blocks.what: Find any sub-step of the six-step process on its own: why it matters, what it produces and its tasks.

building_blocks.name: Controls Catalog
building_blocks.what: Every governance control in one place: the safeguards built into each product, and where each is set, built, proved and watched.

building_blocks.name: Glossary
building_blocks.what: The words we use, one meaning each, so every plan says the same thing, plus the old wording we've retired (the audit fails on any left behind). Ends with the bank's terms still to map.

areas.name: Where things stand
areas.why: What's still open, so I can see at any moment what's waiting on me and what comes next.

parent.what: Everything still open in one log: decisions and reviews waiting on me, work to do, questions for the bank, and what's parked.

areas.name: The job

parent.what: The Principal Applied AI Product Manager posting: what the role owns, what it requires and the tools it names.

children.name: Bank Business Briefing
children.what: How the bank earns money, the corporate segment in depth, and where AI work lines up with each revenue line.

children.name: Credit Market Scan
children.what: What banks and vendors are deploying in the commercial credit process, and how each credit use case lines up with the RM plan's seven core use cases.

children.name: Tech Stack Guide
children.what: Every technology in the job: what it is, how the bank likely uses it, and what I need to know.

children.name: Job Notes
children.what: My answers so far on how I'd do the job, part by part.

areas.name: How I deliver
areas.why: The operating model I'd bring to every AI product: the steps, the machine that runs them, and the manual for doing it.

parent.what: The six steps every product goes through, each with a go/no-go gate, and the rules that keep it governed.

children.name: The Delivery Machine
children.what: How one product manager runs many projects at once: every task marked Auto, Draft, Me or Partner.

children.name: Delivery Playbook
children.what: The field manual: how to run each of the 44 sub-steps the first time, plus the 33 general agents that run the delivery machine. All 39 agents, including the RM product's own 6, are on the Agent Library.

children.name: Six-Step Product Workflow
children.what: A one-page visual of the six steps for the role.

areas.name: Projects
areas.why: Real plans built on the framework. The first is AI-powered analytics for relationship managers.

parent.name: RM Analytics Framework
parent.what: The design page: the one-page summary and the full plan in six parts, side by side.

children.name: RM Analytics Plan
children.what: The same full plan as one continuous scrolling page: the easiest way to read it start to finish.

children.name: McKinsey Use Cases
children.what: Core reference for choosing use cases: McKinsey's five frontline AI use cases and their returns, how the RM plan covers them, and the seven core use cases the RM plan is organized on (McKinsey's five plus admin off the RM's plate and keep clients).
